description: The pie chart visually represents the distribution of attribution evaluation across various domains in the context of large language models, as discussed in the paper “Automatic Evaluation of Attribution by Large Language Models.” It is segmented into 12 distinct categories, each labeled with its corresponding domain and percentage. The largest segment, colored bright blue, represents “AI/NLP Research” at 24.3%, followed by “Econ. & Fin.” in teal at 18.4%. Other notable segments include “History” and “Game&Anime,” both at 8.2%, and “Daily Life” at 7.1%. Smaller segments include “Med & Health” and “Science” (6.7% each), “Pet & Animal” (5.5%), “Law” (5.1%), “Business” (5.9%), “Geography” (2.7%), and “Math” (1.2%). Each slice is clearly labeled with a line pointing to its corresponding percentage and category name, and the chart uses a diverse color palette to distinguish between domains. No slice is exploded or emphasized visually beyond its proportional size, and the segments appear to be arranged roughly in descending order clockwise from the top.
